claims.claim: **Start combined immunosuppression before or at the time of transplant** (1A), and include a biologic induction agent (1B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First-line induction is an IL-2 receptor antagonist** (1B). With high risk of acute cellular rejection, a T-cell-depleting agent may be used instead (2B). A mycophenolate loading dose can be considered (2B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Donor-specific anti-HLA antibody:** consider peri-transplant plasmapheresis and/or high-dose IV immunoglobulin (2C). **ABO-incompatible transplant:** plasmapheresis or immunoadsorption to the titre the unit accepts, with post-transplant antibody removal depending on baseline titre (2A).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintain with a calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) plus an antiproliferative, with or without steroids** (1B); **mycophenolate is the first-line antiproliferative** (1B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tacrolimus is the preferred CNI in higher-risk patients** (2A). Start tacrolimus or ciclosporin before or at transplant, not after graft function begins (2D tacrolimus; 2B ciclosporin).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start an mTOR inhibitor until the graft is working, wounds have healed and there is no rejection** (1B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low immunological risk with induction:** steroids may be minimised or withdrawn early (2B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **By 4 months, move rejection-free patients to low-level exposure** as in the Symphony trial: a tacrolimus trough of 3–7 ng/mL, 1–2 g of mycophenolate a day and 5 mg of prednisone a day (1B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep the CNI rather than withdraw it** (2B); if prednisolone is still used after week one, continue it (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In Australia and New Zealand, most recipients get anti-CD25 induction** (about 95% of transplants in Australia, around 50% in New Zealand) and triple maintenance: a CNI (usually tacrolimus), a mycophenolate and steroids. mTOR inhibitors are used in under 10%.
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Individualise target ranges** to immunological and toxicity risk and co-therapy (2C). Note the assay: immunoassays cross-react with metabolites and usually read higher than HPLC (1B).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure ciclosporin and tacrolimus levels often early on** (for example every second day until stable), after dose changes, after relevant changes in clinical state or interacting drugs, and when over- or under-immunosuppression is suspected (1C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tacrolimus: use trough (C0) levels** (2D). **Ciclosporin:** 12 h trough (C0), 2 h post-dose (C2), or a validated limited sampling strategy (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mycophenolate levels are not routine** but may help in selected cases (high immunological risk, interacting changes, suspected over- or under-immunosuppression). Early target mycophenolic acid AUC0–12: 30 to 60 mg·h/L; no target is known beyond 12 months (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor mTOR inhibitor blood levels** (1C) after starting or changing dose, with suspected interactions, or when immunosuppression seems excessive or inadequate; trough levels can be used, but targets vary by drug, rejection risk and time since transplant (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Biopsy before treating acute rejection unless it would substantially delay treatment** (1C). Treat subclinical and borderline cellular rejection too (2D).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute cellular rejection: first give a short course of high-dose steroids** (1D), and add back maintenance prednisone in patients not on it (2D). Use lymphocyte-depleting antibody for resistant rejection or vascular rejection (Banff grade II or more) (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antibody-mediated rejection:** consider plasma exchange and/or IV immunoglobulin (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After any rejection, step up baseline immunosuppression:** add mycophenolate or switch azathioprine to it; add a CNI; switch ciclosporin to tacrolimus or an mTOR inhibitor to a CNI; or raise doses (2D).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biopsy any graft with falling function of unclear cause** to find reversible causes (1C). With CNI toxicity on histology, reduce, stop or replace the CNI (2C); swap to an mTOR inhibitor only if eGFR is over 40 mL/min per 1.73 m2 with urine protein under 50 mg/mmol creatinine, and not when eGFR is below 40 (2D).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check serum creatinine often** (1B): at least daily for 7 days or until discharge, two to three times weekly in weeks 2–4, weekly in months 2 and 3, every 2 weeks in months 4–6, monthly in months 7–12, then every 2–3 months. Check urine PCR or ACR once in month one, every 3 months in year one, then annually (2C).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biopsy when creatinine rises persistently without explanation** (1C), when it fails to return to baseline after rejection treatment (2D), with new or unexplained proteinuria (2C), every 5–10 days during delayed graft function (2C), or if expected function is not reached by 1–2 months (2D).
claims.locator: KHA-CARI (Chadban SJ et al.), Nephrology, 'KHA-CARI guideline: KHA-CARI adaptation of the KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Care of Kidney Transplant Recipients (summary, Nephrology 2012; 17: 204–214)', published 2012 (accepted December 2011); listed as current (Jan 2012) on the CARI Transplant page, https://www.cariguidelines.org/wp-content/uploads/Transplantation/transplantation%20care%20of%20recipients/Summaries/Chadban_2012_204.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
